clue.text: French writer returns money with bill

indicators.note: returns tells us the whole run of money and bill is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A French author sends back some cash together with the invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns SUM + AC round as one run, giving CAMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French novelist and philosopher, author of The Outsider.

clue.text: Fish makes old-fashioned bow before dance.

parts.note: a conge is an archaic word for a ceremonious bow
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A fish bows in the old style before a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: CONGE is an archaic word for a formal bow on taking leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger eel is a large marine eel, a sea fish.

clue.text: Cut is in fashion, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for fashion is said out loud to give a word sounding alike

parts.note: mode means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A haircut is trendy, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: MODE said out loud sounds like MOWED; 'is in' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Mowed means cut, as grass with a mower.

clue.text: Broken tape recorder at the Olympics?

definitions.text: Broken tape recorder at the Olympics?

parts.words: Broken tape recorder at the Olympics?
parts.note: the tape is the finishing line breasted by a winning runner, and the device records the time when it is broken

explanation.surface: A faulty cassette machine at the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken tape recorder' suggests a faulty cassette player; the tape is the finishing line, and the device that records when it is broken is the official's timer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held timer used by athletics officials records each runner's time as they break the finishing line.

clue.text: To do with an art, perhaps, involving Celt china

definitions.text: To do with an art, perhaps

indicators.note: involving in its sense of tangling up or rolling together signals the letters of Celt china are mixed

explanation.surface: Something artistic, perhaps, featuring Celtic pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' looks like a container signal, but here it means entangling: the nine letters of CELT CHINA are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical means relating to a particular skill or craft, of which an art is one example.

clue.text: Comprises cheats

explanation.surface: It consists of fraudsters.
explanation.walkthrough: Takes in means both includes and deceives.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in is to include or contain; it also means to deceive or fool someone.

clue.text: Garland Nora gathered-in the pass

indicators.note: in places the shuffled name within the mountain pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: gathered suggests the letters of Nora are pulled together into a new order

explanation.surface: Nora picks up a garland while crossing the pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' rearranges NORA to RONA, which goes 'in' COL.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronal is a circlet or wreath worn on the head.

clue.text: Near to half time

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word to leaves its opening letter

explanation.surface: Getting on for the interval in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half time' looks like a phrase, the interval in a game; but 'half' works on 'to', leaving T, and 'time' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness between dusk and dawn.

clue.text: Look over the track for the meeting

parts.note: to con is to study or examine
a course is a racetrack

explanation.surface: Inspecting the racetrack before a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old word meaning study or peruse.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a crowd gathering together, a coming together of people.

clue.text: Goes on to make a final point

parts.note: last means final
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone keeps talking to make a closing remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, S; 'to make a' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasts means continues or endures.

clue.text: Gothamite periodical

explanation.surface: A magazine for Gotham's citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: Gotham is a nickname for New York City, so a Gothamite is its resident; the second sense is the famous weekly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gothamite lives in Gotham, nickname of Manhattan's city; and a well-known weekly magazine carries that title too.

clue.text: A kind of information of service to the country

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
US, the United States, is the usual crossword country

explanation.surface: Some sort of intelligence useful to the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of service to' is a link joining the pieces; GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus is a class or sort, especially in biological classification.

clue.text: Invest with some friend owning a business?

indicators.note: with some says only part of the following words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Fund a pal who owns a firm?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'friEND OWning'.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to invest someone with a quality or provide them with funds.

clue.text: Authorizes penalties?

explanation.surface: Officials give approval and impose fines.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has opposite senses: as a verb it permits, as a plural noun it means punitive measures.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to approve; sanctions are also punitive measures, as against a state.

clue.text: Clergyman is back in school football club

indicators.note: in places the reversed clergyman inside the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: is back says the clergyman's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar returns to his old school's football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is back' turns REV into VER, which goes 'in' ETON. Everton is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is an English football club based in Liverpool.

clue.text: Natives regret upset over work with E.N.S.A. members

indicators.note: upset says the pooled letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: to rue is to regret
op is short for opus, a work
the members of E.N.S.A. are its four letters, ENSA being the wartime forces entertainment body

explanation.surface: Locals regret disruption of a show by wartime entertainers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' shuffles RUE, OP and ENSA together. ENSA was Britain's wartime Entertainments National Service Association.
explanation.definitionFit: Europeans are people born in or native to Europe.

clue.text: Looked sullen when let down?

explanation.surface: Someone scowled when they were disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: To lower (also spelt lour) is to frown or look sullen; lowered is also simply the past of lower, let down.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour or lower is to scowl darkly; and something lowered has been brought down.

clue.text: Classic definition of a quid -known by the well-informed

explanation.surface: A pound's meaning is something insiders know.
explanation.walkthrough: In Latin ('Classic'), quid means 'what', so its definition is 'what': the phrase says what 'what' is. 'Quid' looks like British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing the true state of affairs is knowing how things really stand; and Latin quid translates as the English word what.

clue.text: Devilish habit to break up!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, the devil's realm
a habit is a garment, as is a mantle or cloak

explanation.surface: A diabolical custom to destroy!
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' means a garment, not a custom; Dis is the Roman ruler of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take apart, to pull something into pieces.

clue.text: Dog performing staggering feats?

explanation.surface: A dog doing amazing tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' means not amazing but reeling: one who lurches. A lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog; read literally, the word is one who reels or sways.

clue.text: Determine to do your work again?

explanation.surface: Decide to redo your homework.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SOLVE, it means solve once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to decide firmly; read as re-solve it means work out a puzzle a second time.

clue.text: Journeys give Val rest and change

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of Val rest are switched around

explanation.surface: Trips give Val a break and a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and change' rearranges the seven letters of VAL REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Travels are trips or journeys, especially long ones.

clue.text: Wearisome duties — nothing varied

indicators.note: varied says the letters are changed into a different order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Tiresome chores with no variety at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges DUTIES plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious describes something dull and tiring because it goes on too long.

clue.text: 15 papers indeed!

indicators.note: the in of indeed places the newspapers within the deed

parts.note: a deed is an act or legal document
the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'indeed' as 'in deed': PRESS goes inside DEED. The definition is the answer to 15 across, LOWERED, in its sense of downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or let down means being dejected and gloomy.

clue.text: Most important journalist turns up at HQ

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: top means foremost or most important
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: The chief reporter arrives at headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses TOP + ED together in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a base or headquarters, as of a regiment.

clue.text: Call up girl about letters expressing agreement

indicators.note: about tells us the girl's name surrounds the two letters

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
OK is two letters saying yes, all right

explanation.surface: Phone a girl about a letter of consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call up' looks like phoning; it means bring to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon up a memory or feeling.

clue.text: Capital furniture around one?

indicators.note: around says the furniture encloses the figure one

parts.note: a sofa is an item of furniture
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Smart furniture surrounding someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like an adjective meaning excellent; it is the city, capital of Bulgaria.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Very light food when about fifty

indicators.note: about says the food goes round the numeral

parts.note: fare is food
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A very low-calorie meal for a fifty-year-old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very light' looks like 'extremely light'; a Very light is a signal flare fired from a pistol. 'when' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is a coloured signal shot from a pistol, named after its inventor Edward Very.

clue.text: Quietly sanctimonious article on retirement

parts.note: pi is slang for piously self-righteous
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: retirement, drawing back, says the word on is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hushed, self-righteous newspaper piece about stopping work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns ON into NO, after PI and A. PI is short for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, piano is the direction to play softly.

clue.text: Beastly organ pieces composed by Richard

parts.note: the lion is king of the beasts, so beastly here suggests that animal
the heart is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: Awful organ music composed by a man named Richard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces composed by' says the two parts make up Richard's epithet: King Richard I of England was called the Lionheart.
explanation.definitionFit: King Richard I of England is known by the epithet Lionheart, Coeur de Lion.

clue.text: Insipid Hardy 'character without the least eccentricity

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the Hardy heroine encloses the rest

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

indicators.note: eccentricity, oddness, signals the letters of least are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dull Hardy figure who has not the slightest oddness about her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: TESS wraps ASTEL, the anagram of LEAST from 'eccentricity', split T...ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tasteless has no flavour, which is to say bland and flat.

clue.text: Where's the note?

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Asking where a note has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is used as it stands and RE is the sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: There names a place in answer to a question of location: in that spot.
